newsitem.title: USA: Kantor-data show better long-term US trade picture.
newsitem.headline: Kantor-data show better long-term US trade picture.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor Wednesday said data show prospects for long-term improvement in the U.S. trade picture despite the sharp rise in the U.S. trade deficit in July.
"Despite the one-month fall-off in July, today's data speak to the prospects for long-term improvement in the U.S. trade picture," Kantor said at a news conference.

He said the gap with Japan for the first seven months of 1996 is 29 percent below the level in the same 1995 period. He cited rising U.S. exports to Japan, particularly in autos, which he said grew by 256 percent between 1992 and 1995.
Kantor said the U.S. trade picture with Mexico has stabilized, and noted that the deficit fell for the second month in a row in July.
He expressed concern about the trade deficit with China, and said that it was up nine percent so far this year.
"We are deeply concerned about the deficit with China simply because it is the result of sanctuary markets," Kantor said.
But he said the growth of the U.S. trade deficit with China "is substantially below the growth rate of recent years."
Kantor also cited the strong U.S. economy compared to the economies of its key trading partners -- Canada, Europe, Japan and Mexico.
He said the U.S. economy over the past four years has been the strongest of the G7 economies.
"I think the recovery (of other G7 economies) has been slower than any one would have expected or wanted," Kantor said.
